data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --partition cpulong
#   --nodes 1
#   --ntasks-per-node 1
#   --mem-per-cpu 8G
#   --time 3-0:00:00
#   --job-name sweep
#   --output slogs/sweep-%J.log

#flux: --job-name=sweep
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=72h

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu 8G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --partition cpulong
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different limits/priority (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: --output slogs/sweep-%J.log
# Slurm's %J/%j token expansion is not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose a unique filename.

module purge

singularity exec ${OPENSPIEL_IMG} wandb agent ${WANDB_PROJECT}

reasons: The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu 8G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.

The original Slurm job specified a partition (`--partition cpulong`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
